subhead: The first visitors admired the Bayeux Tapestry at the British Museum on Thursday. The work is on loan from France to the United Kingdom until July 2027. Public interest reflects both the importance of William the Conqueror's accession to the English throne in the national story and the fascination of seeing a nearly 1,000-year-old tapestry.

title: French economy falls behind rest of Europe: Slow growth, rising inflation and unemployment
subhead: Growth is not expected to exceed 0.4% in 2026, down from the previously forecast 0.7%, according to the French National Institute of Statistics and Economic Studies. The main drivers of demand – consumer spending and investment – have stalled, while inflation and unemployment continue to rise.

title: 2030 Alps Games: Organizing committee chief resigns after turbulent 10-month tenure

title: China's forbidden memory of the greatest famine in history
subhead: 'Mao's Fraught Legacy' (2/7). The Great Leap Forward, imposed on China by Mao Zedong from 1958 to 1961, triggered one of the deadliest famines in human history. In rural areas, especially in Henan province, where peasants paid the heaviest price for this economic policy, the topic remains taboo.
